Bill.BriefDescription: Regulating water availability for residential fire sprinkler suppression systems.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to providing water for residential fire sprinklersuppression systems; adding new sections to chapter 35.21 RCW; addingnew sections to chapter 35A.21 RCW; and adding a new section to chapter36.94 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 35.21 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: When a water supply for builtin automatic residential firesprinkler suppression systems is installed by a property owner orsystem contractor in a residence: (1) The property owner or system contractor shall not be subject tothe imposition of additional meter charges by a municipality or waterdistrict when flow and pressure requirements dictate that a largerwater supply is necessary, and standard residential water pricingschedules shall be imposed by the municipality or water district; (2) The property owner or system contractor shall not be subject tothe imposition of water system development assessments by themunicipality or water district; and p. 1 SHB 2845 (3) The water must be supplied from a single metered connection tothe municipal or water district system and the connection must be sizedto supply both domestic and fire sprinkler system requirements.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 35A.21 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: When a water supply for builtin automatic residential firesprinkler suppression systems is installed by a property owner orsystem contractor in a residence: (1) The property owner or system contractor shall not be subject tothe imposition of additional meter charges by a code city or waterdistrict when flow and pressure requirements dictate that a largerwater supply is necessary, and standard residential water pricingschedules shall be imposed by the code city or water district; (2) The property owner or system contractor shall not be subject tothe imposition of water system development assessments by the code cityor water district; and (3) The water must be supplied from a single metered connection tothe code city or water district system and the connection must be sizedto supply both domestic and fire sprinkler system requirements.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 36.94 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Water systems operating under this chapter are prohibited fromrequiring residential water customers to pay a water serviceavailability charge, standby charge, consumption charge, or any othersimilar types of charges associated with available but unused waterservice, including any interest or penalties for nonpayment orenforcement charges, when the water connection is installed for builtin automatic fire sprinkler suppression systems.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 35.21 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Cities and towns are prohibited from requiring residential watercustomers to pay a water service availability charge, standby charge,consumption charge, or any other similar types of charges associatedwith available but unused water service, including any interest or SHB 2845 p. 2 penalties for nonpayment or enforcement charges, when the waterconnection is installed for builtin automatic fire sprinklersuppression systems.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 35A.21 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Code cities are prohibited from requiring residential watercustomers to pay a water service availability charge, standby charge,consumption charge, or any other similar types of charges associatedwith available but unused water service, including any interest orpenalties for nonpayment or enforcement charges, when the waterconnection is installed for builtin automatic fire sprinklersuppression systems.
